https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/08/14/megh.text: Menü Kereső Meghívta Paksra Orbán Viktort és a többi parlamenti párt elnökét Magyar Péter Belföld Cseke Balázs Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Szombat délelőtt 10 órára meghívta Paksra a parlamenti pártok elnökeit Magyar Péter. A miniszterelnök Facebook-posztja szerint azért várja Orbán Viktort (Fidesz), Semjén Zsoltot (KDNP) és Toroczkai Lászlót (Mi Hazánk), hogy tájékoztassa őket „az évtizedek óta nem látott építkezés részleteiről, továbbá a korábbi évek mulasztásairól, amelyek szükségessé tették a beavatkozást”. A szerdai kormányülésen döntöttek arról , hogy több lépésben igyekeznek megoldani a Duna alacsony vízállását a Paksi Atomerőműnél, hogy biztosítani tudják a turbinák működését. Elrendelték a fenékküszöb építését, amelyhez összesen 145 ezer köbméter követ fognak a Dunába önteni. Oké, de mégis mi az a fenékküszöb? Itt írtunk róla bővebben. Amíg az megépül, ideiglenes megoldásként két 80 méteres bárkát helyeznek készenlétbe Paksnál, amiket bármikor el tudnak süllyeszteni. A teljes beruházás a becsülések szerint hatmilliárd forintba kerül. Magyar Péter a csütörtöki sajtótájékoztatón ismertette részletesebben , hogyan nézne ki az építés folyamata. Arról is beszélt, hogy a nulláról kellett elkészítenie a kormánynak a paksi terveket, mert az előző kormány nem készült a jelenlegi helyzetre. A Telex kérdésére úgy fogalmazott, hogy emiatt személyi és intézményi felelősség is felmerülhet az Orbán-kormány idejéből. A Fidesz és a KDNP szerint ugyanakkor ezt a válságot az okozza, hogy Magyar Péterék nem készültek fel rá. Augusztus elején a köztársasági elnök jogait gyakorló Forshoffer Ágnes hívta meg a Sándor-palotába Magyart és a parlamenti pártok frakcióvezetőit. Akkor jó két órát egyeztettek zárt ajtók mögött. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/a.text: Vladimir Putin in Moscow this week. Russia has made frequent threats against Ukraine’s western allies. Photograph: Mikhail Metzel/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Vladimir Putin in Moscow this week. Russia has made frequent threats against Ukraine’s western allies. Photograph: Mikhail Metzel/AFP/Getty Images Russia Russia says UK ‘playing with fire’ amid reports CIA chief has warned Kremlin not to attack Nato Moscow threatens retaliation after Andy Burnham says UK will help Ukraine start producing long-range missiles Peter Beaumont and Jessica Elgot Thu 27 Aug 2026 12.56 EDT First published on Thu 27 Aug 2026 07.34 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Russia has said it could retaliate against the UK for its support of Kyiv by striking military targets inside and outside Ukraine , amid reports that the director of the CIA warned the Kremlin against attacking Nato during a secretive visit this week. Andy Burnham, Britain’s prime minister, said on Monday the UK would allow Kyiv access to classified technology to start ⁠its own production of Storm Shadow ​long-range ​cruise missiles. France has also agreed to supply missile technology. Maria ⁠Zakharova, Russia’s foreign ministry spokesperson, said on Thursday Britain and France were “playing ⁠with ​fire”. Responding to the latest Russian threats, a Ministry of Defence official reiterated UK support for Ukraine. “Britain stands shoulder to shoulder with Ukraine and we are committed to providing the equipment Ukraine needs to defend itself against Putin’s illegal invasion. Russia should be in no doubt about the resolve of this government to stand against Russian aggression, in Ukraine and against the UK and our allies,” they said. The Wall Street Journal reported that a visit by John Ratcliffe, the CIA chief, to Moscow on Tuesday had followed a US intelligence assessment that Russia could be planning to test Nato with a limited assault on an allied country. This could range from a cyber-attack to a small-scale incursion, probably in a Baltic nation. Russia has made frequent threats against Ukraine’s western allies during the war, including thinly veiled nuclear threats and others apparently aimed at diplomatic missions in Kyiv. View image in fullscreen K2 Black Panther main battle tanks will be deployed by Poland near the border with Russia’s Kaliningrad region as Nato countries neighbouring Russia move to increase their military readiness. Photograph: Roman Koziel/Zuma Press Wire/Shutterstock Asked ‌to comment ‌on the reports of Ratcliffe’s visit – and despite Thursday morning’s threat against UK targets – Dmitry Peskov, the Kremlin spokesperson, said: “A lot of this kind of scare-story material is being published right now. Of course, it has ‌nothing to do with reality and nothing to do ​with the intentions of the Russian Federation.” The intense scrutiny around the Ratcliffe trip and Russia’s intentions comes amid a new report over shortfalls of missile interceptors available in Europe . A report by the Associated Press says the US military is experiencing a “beyond critical” shortage of advanced missile interceptors in Europe largely driven by Donald Trump’s war with Iran, according to a US defence official in Europe and a Nato official, raising concerns about vulnerabilities in Nato countries to a potential Russian attack. The US defence official said the most concerning shortfall involved Patriot missile interceptors, which can shoot down Russia’s high-speed ballistic missiles. The Nato official confirmed the low inventories of Patriots among American and Nato forces in Europe. Both spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive military matters. Russia is believed to be contemplating a further escalation of its war with Ukraine after months of escalating Ukrainian attacks on Russia’s oil refining infrastructure and other sites, which are imposing an increasing economic toll. View image in fullscreen A Japanese government sign in Tokyo says ‘the Northern Territories are an inherent part of Japan’s territory’, referring to the Russian-controlled Southern Kuril Islands. Russia has invoked its nuclear threat against Japan over the claim. Photograph: Yuichi Yamazaki/AFP/Getty Images The Kremlin has adopted ever more bellicose rhetoric, much of it aimed at a domestic audience, as the war in Ukraine has been brought to its doorstep. In the space of a few days Russia has invoked the threat of its nuclear arsenal against Japan over its territorial claim to the disputed Kuril Islands. It has described relations with the US as a “crisis” and at a historic low point. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every day Sign up to Headlines Europe A digest of the morning's main headlines from the Europe edition emailed direct to you every week day after newsletter promotion Ratcliffe’s reported warning mirrored one made by his predecessor, William Burns, in 2021 before Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine – which Moscow also denied it was contemplating. Concerns over Moscow’s intentions have been increasing amid a rise in incidents of Russian hybrid warfare attributed to Moscow across Europe, from cyber-attacks and drones to arson, at facilities associated with supporting Ukraine’s war efforts. Russia and the US have tried to play down Ratcliffe’s meeting with his Russian counterparts: Donald Trump on Wednesday described the visit as “semi routine”. However, the unusual nature of the encounter has caused intense speculation in the west and Russia. Nato countries neighbouring Russia have moved quickly to increase their military readiness. Poland this week announced it had taken delivery of its first shipment of South Korean Black Panther main battle tanks, which will be deployed near the border with Russia’s Kaliningrad region. Cezary Tomczyk, Poland’s deputy defence minister, said this month Warsaw was preparing for the possibility of a full-scale conflict. Tomczyk told Super Express media : “We are preparing for war, hoping it never happens.” Explore more on these topics Russia Ukraine Nato Poland Europe news Share Reuse this content More on this story More on this story Yorkshireman believed to be first Briton to die fighting for Russia against Ukraine UK officials prepare for potential Trump talks as Burnham plans New York trip Burnham’s visit to Kyiv marks a renewal of badly needed support for Ukraine Burnham says UK with Ukraine ‘all the way’ despite ‘outrageous threats’ from Russia – Europe live Burnham accuses Russia of ‘outrageous threats’ against UK as he visits Kyiv On Donetsk’s ‘life or death’ highway with the Khyzhak brigade – photo essay The Audio Long Read ‘The war leaked into every lesson’: learning Ukrainian in a country under siege – podcast Ukraine war briefing: Nord Stream bombings were not us, Zelenskyy insists Russia withdraws ambassador to UK as Kremlin raises pressure over Ukraine support Most viewed Most viewed World Europe US news Americas Asia Australia Middle East Africa Inequality Global development

https://www.theguardian.com/australia-ne.text: Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom, one of the seven World Central Kitchen colleagues killed in an Israeli airstrike in Gaza. Photograph: World Central Kitchen/PA View image in fullscreen Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom, one of the seven World Central Kitchen colleagues killed in an Israeli airstrike in Gaza. Photograph: World Central Kitchen/PA Australian foreign policy Shoebridge criticises Labor response after IDF officer’s ‘reprehensible’ comments on deadly Zomi Frankcom strike Greens defence spokesman says ‘words are just distractions’ until government takes action ‘Guilt by association’: why seven international aid workers were killed in Israeli airstrike Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Ben Doherty Sun 6 Sep 2026 11.00 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The Greens have criticised inflammatory statements from the former Israel Defense Forces officer who ordered the attack which killed Zomi Frankcom, accusing the Albanese government of weakness over its failure to halt military exports and impose new sanctions. Australian aid worker Frankcom and six of her colleagues were killed in 2024 while bringing food to the people of Gaza . Former IDF reserve colonel Nochi Mendel has said he would do “exactly the same thing” again and that those killed in the World Central Kitchen (WCK) humanitarian convoy in Gaza were “not innocent”. The statements have been condemned as “utterly disgraceful” by Australia’s foreign affairs minister, Penny Wong, and as an “outrageous smear” by WCK’s humanitarian chief. Death on the road to Rafah: the night the IDF targeted World Central Kitchen aid workers Read more But the Greens’ defence spokesperson, David Shoebridge, said the government’s response was insufficient in the face of Mendel’s “reprehensible” statements. He said the comments “reflect the rhetoric and policy of the Israeli government, where collective punishment of aid workers, doctors and innocent civilians is occurring daily”. “I do not care what minister Wong’s personal feelings are, I don’t care about her outrage, I care about the actions taken as foreign minister,” Shoebridge told Guardian Australia. “Anyone can condemn the actions of the Israeli military, but only the government can impose the sanctions and material responses needed. Until they do their words are distractions.” He called for material reprimand for members of Benjamin Netanyahu’s government and for the sale of parts for the F-35 fighter jet to be immediately halted. View image in fullscreen The Greens’ defence spokesperson, David Shoebridge, said on Sunday he could not fathom the pain and distress facing Zomi Frankcom’s family. Photograph: Lukas Coch/AAP José Andrés, the WCK founder, said Mendel had smeared Frankcom and her colleagues. “Now, one of the officers involved says he isn’t sorry for what happened. He said we are not a neutral organisation,” he said in a statement published online this week. “Really? Let me be very clear, to him and to the whole world. We are humanitarians. We are friends of humanity. We believe that food is a universal human right.” Mendel, then the chief of staff of the Nahal brigade, said he gave the order to attack a humanitarian convoy delivering hundreds of tonnes of food to Gaza on the night of 1 April 2024. Three vehicles in the convoy were attacked along Gaza’s coast road, in successive drone strikes, each about two minutes apart. One after another, the three vehicles were bombed, as survivors from the initial strikes ran to the untouched cars, seeking sanctuary. An IDF investigation found the attack was a grave mistake, identifying specific errors made by a handful of officers, in particular Mendel, who was removed from his position. The victims of the strike were also blamed for hiring armed guards to protect the food aid convoy and for allegedly “deviating” from their agreed route. ‘An insult’: Zomi Frankcom’s family issues strongly-worded statement as Israel rejects criminal investigation into her killing Read more Last month, Israel’s advocate general declined to press charges against anyone for the deaths, saying there was “no reasonable suspicion of criminal misconduct”. Mendel has given interviews to the ABC and the Guardian saying he did not regret the attacks. He told the Guardian he was following IDF protocol, and the humanitarians were marked as targets under an Israeli military practice of establishing guilt by association . Mendel was referring to a general policy of haflala , “incrimination”, which gives commanders in the field wide discretion in designating a person a “terrorist”, including those “incriminated” by association. Mendel told the Guardian while he didn’t plan to kill aid workers, those killed “were not innocent because they were connected to Hamas”. He did not support this assertion with any evidence. Investigations by the IDF itself and the former head of the Australian military have found no suggestion of any connection between Hamas and World Central Kitchen. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion View image in fullscreen A destroyed car from the World Central Kitchen convoy in the southern Gaza Strip. Photograph: Mohammed Saber/EPA Mendel said he fought in the war in Gaza “to defeat Hamas”, and dismissed the seriousness of the killing of seven humanitarians. “If such an event came before me again, I would do exactly the same thing,” he told the Guardian. “I think it’s an idiotic side event. It really isn’t a serious event.” Wong, asked about earlier comments from Mendel that he was unapologetic over the strikes, said his statements were extremely distressing for Frankcom’s family. “I thought those comments were disgraceful, utterly disgraceful,” she told the ABC. “I don’t even want to go into some of the detail of them because I don’t want to give them any credence.” Wong said the Australian government was dissatisfied with Israel’s decision not to lay criminal charges against those responsible, and would continue to “press for justice”. “We do want to see full accountability for the deaths of Zomi Frankcom and her colleagues. They were humanitarian workers working to deliver aid and they are protected under the Geneva conventions.” Wong 'outraged' at Israeli decision to not criminally investigate Zomi Frankcom killing – video Restaurateur Andrés, whose charity has provided more than 600m meals to people affected by natural disasters, climate emergencies and conflict around the world, said the deaths of humanitarian workers who were just trying to feed hungry people was inexcusable. “Enough with the outrageous smears. Enough with excuses. Enough with the shifting of blame. “From the start, we have demanded truth, truth and justice for our friends and their families. We want an independent investigation with all the video and audio released in public so the world can know the truth, because we continue to grieve for our friends. We will never forget them or stop fighting for them.” Frankcom’s family issued a statement following Israel’s decision not to lay criminal charges , saying they were “deeply disappointed” by the decision. “The families of the victims deserve transparency and an independent judicial assessment of the criminal responsibility for the international humanitarian law violations that took place on that day,” the said. Shoebridge said on Sunday he could not fathom the pain and distress facing the Frankcom family. “I think most people are in shock at the inaction of the Labor government when an Australian has been murdered and the killers walk free. At some point the Albanese government is going to have to get their head out of sand and start taking action.” Explore more on these topics Australian foreign policy Israel-Gaza war Australian Greens Israel news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed World Europe US news Americas Asia Australia Middle East Africa Inequality Global development

https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/09/23/orsz.text: Menü Kereső „Bízunk a férfi mielőbbi felépülésében” – írták Facebookjukon a mentők egy férfiról, majd a felesége odakommentelte, hogy aznap volt a temetése Belföld Iván-Nagy Szilvia Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom „A bejegyzést kegyeleti okból módosítottuk. Osztozunk a család fájdalmában, őszinte részvétünket fejezzük ki a hozzátartozóknak!” – áll az Országos Mentőszolgálat egyik, kedden este módosított Facebook-bejegyzésének végén, amit azután módosítottak, hogy a sikertörténetként közzétett bejegyzéshez a kórházba szállított férfi felesége azt írta: férje szeptember 6-án meghalt, kedden temették. A módosítást elsőként a 444.hu vette észre. Az eredeti, kedden napközben publikált szövegben a mentőszolgálat arról írt, hogy különös hangra figyelt fel egy nő Pest megyei otthonuk hálószobájában, ahol 40 év körüli férje pihent. A nő ezután hamar a mentők segítségét kérte, mert nem tudta felébreszteni a férjét. A bejegyzés szerint a férfihoz riasztották a mentőket, a nőt pedig újraélesztésre instruálták. A férfit kórházba vitték, miközben folyamatosan próbálták újraéleszteni, a bejegyzést pedig azzal zárták, hogy „a gyors szállítást követően megtartott keringéssel adták át bajtársaink a beteget a kórházban, ahol újabb életmentő beavatkozások vártak rá. Bízunk a férfi mielőbbi felépülésében, bajtársainknak szívből gratulálunk!” Az eredeti, kedden délután fél négy körül megosztott bejegyzéshez 18:30-kor a történetben szereplő férfi felesége írt kommentet: „Az én férjem volt, sajnos szeptember 6-án elhunyt!! Ma volt a temetése😭😭😭😭😭 sajnos, későn sikerült az újraélesztés!!” És kommentelt a nő testvére, a férfi sógora is. Az Országos Mentőszolgálat az özvegy kommentjére azt írta, őszinte részvétüket fejezik ki számára és az egész család számára: „osztozunk a fájdalmukban”. A bejegyzés alatt többen is megfogalmaztak kritikát az Országos Mentőszolgálattal szemben a tartalom miatt. Az egyik kommentelő, aki mentődolgozóként hivatkozott magára, azt vetette fel, hogy „változtatni kellene az elmúlt évek azon gyakorlatán is, miszerint a mentőszolgálat sokszor edukációs vagy egyéb hasznos érték nélküli eseteket posztol a közösségi médiában, látszólag pusztán a nagyobb elérés kiharcolása érdekében”. Szerinte más emberek tragédiáját ilyen céllal felhasználni etikátlan, még akkor is, ha a poszt írója és a közzétételt jóváhagyó döntéshozó nem rossz szándékkal teszi mindezt. Kommentjére a mentőszolgálat is reagált. Megköszönték a kritikát, és azt, hogy őszintén fogalmazta meg a véleményét. „A hozzátartozók visszajelzése ebben az esetben számunkra is megmutatta, hogy egy anonimizált történet is felismerhetővé válhat a család számára. A bejegyzést ezért módosítottuk.” Azt is írták, hogy az esetek bemutatásával a dolgozók szakmai munkáját és elhivatottságát szeretnék megmutatni, „és sok történet arra is rámutat, milyen fontos szerepe lehet a laikusok gyors felismerésének, segítségkérésének és az életmentés megkezdésének. Ez azonban csak kellő körültekintéssel, az érintettek és hozzátartozóik méltóságának tiszteletben tartásával vállalható.” Zárásként kitértek rá, hogy a történteket a saját kommunikációs gyakorlatuk szempontjából is tanulságként kezelik.
